title: Local Architect vs. National Firm for Your Scarsdale Home Project
excerpt: When you're planning a renovation or addition in Scarsdale, you have choices about who designs and builds your project. Here's what matters most when deciding between a local architect and a national firm.
content:
If you're thinking about renovating your kitchen, adding a second story, or building an addition in Scarsdale, one of your first decisions is who to hire. You might consider a national firm with offices across the country, or you might work with someone local. Both options exist. The real question is which one makes sense for your specific project and your home.

The answer isn't the same for everyone. It depends on what you're trying to accomplish, how much attention you want during the process, and what kind of relationship matters to you. Let's break down the differences so you can decide what's right for you.

Why a Local Architect Knows Your Market

A residential architect in Scarsdale who actually lives and works in your community has spent years understanding the area. That's not a small thing. Your architect knows the neighborhoods. They know what works architecturally in Scarsdale. They've worked with your local building department multiple times. They understand the permit process because they've been through it many times before.

When you work with a local firm like ours here in Eastchester, your architect isn't learning about Scarsdale while working on your project. They've already done renovations, additions, and custom homes in similar homes throughout Westchester County. They know which contractors in the area are reliable. They know the local inspectors and code officials.

This familiarity saves time. It reduces surprises. It means your project moves forward without someone halfway across the country trying to figure out how Scarsdale's building department works.

The Personal Relationship With a Design-Build Firm

When you hire a licensed architect in New York who is also a general contractor, something shifts. The person designing your addition is the same person overseeing its construction. That's the design-build model, and it changes how a project runs.

In our firm, Silvio M. Luca is both the architect and the contractor. He runs every project personally. You're not handed off from one team to another. You're not dealing with a designer in one office and a contractor in another state. The person who drew your plans is the person managing the build. That means the design actually gets built the way it was intended.

This matters during construction. When questions come up, your architect-contractor can make decisions without delay. When something needs adjustment, the person making that call understands both the design intent and the practical reality of building.

National Firms Have Their Place Too

A large national architecture firm brings resources. They might have specialists in certain building types. They might have extensive software systems or research teams. For some clients, that appeals to them.

But there are tradeoffs. Your project is one of hundreds or thousands across the country. Your local Scarsdale home is probably not the focus of the principal architect. You'll likely work with associates or junior staff. The design might come from people who've never been to Westchester. Your contractor could be someone unfamiliar with local building codes or the Scarsdale permitting process.

Coordination happens through emails and calls across time zones. If something goes wrong, solutions take longer to implement.

What You Should Do Next

Start by thinking about what matters most to you. Do you want someone who knows Scarsdale and your neighborhood? Do you want your architect and contractor to be the same person? Or do you prefer the resources and name recognition of a larger firm?
